findings.title: Per-client resource shadows all-clients permissions
findings.body: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) looks up the resource for the specific client; only if that resource is null does it fall back to the "Clients" all-resource. This means that as soon as any per-client resource exists (e.g. created because someone once granted VIEW on that client), all permissions granted via the all-clients resource are ignored for that client. Concretely, an administrator who was granted MANAGE on all clients via an all-clients permission will lose MANAGE (and CONFIGURE, which delegates to canManage) for a client that merely has a separate per-client VIEW permission. The two resources should be evaluated with OR semantics, or the all-clients grant must still be consulted when the per-client evaluation does not grant the requested scope.

findings.title: Missing null check on all-clients resource can cause NPE
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, scope), AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) can return null (e.g. if the realm does not support the schema, or the "Clients" all-resource was never created). The returned value is then passed to policyStore.findByResource(server, null) and, if non-empty, to new ResourcePermission(null, resource.getScopes(), ...), which will throw. The sibling method hasPermission(String) correctly guards with `if (resource == null) return false;`, but this method does not, so a missing all-clients resource results in a 500 instead of a permission denial.

findings.title: Existing realms never receive the new Clients resource and scopes
findings.body: init() returns immediately when the admin-permissions client already exists. Realms whose admin-permissions client was created before the CLIENTS resource type was introduced will therefore never get the new "Clients" resource, nor the new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) added to resourceServerRep.setScopes(...). Creating a client permission in such a realm will then fail — either the per-client resource creation throws ModelException("No scopes found.") because getOrCreateResource cannot find the scope, or scope validation in getScope rejects the request — and evaluation will hit the null all-clients resource path. A migration/backfill is needed to create any missing schema scopes/resources for realms that already have the client.

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve Clients resources
findings.body: getResourceName special-cases only the USERS resource type (returning "All users" for the type resource and the username for a per-user resource). For the newly added CLIENTS resource type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Per-client FGAP resources are named with the client's internal UUID (see getOrCreateResource/resolveClient) and do not set a display name, so listings of client permissions will show a blank/incorrect name instead of the client's clientId. Add a CLIENTS branch that resolves the client (and an "All clients" label for the type resource) analogously to the USERS branch.

findings.title: Listener guard does not prevent V2 UnsupportedOperationException
findings.body: The listener body is now gated only on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1). But when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is also enabled, management(...) returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled(...) throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). In a realm configured with both features, removing a client (ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent), role, or group will therefore hit role()/clients()/groups().setPermissionsEnabled(...) and fail. The guard should also exclude the V2 case (e.g. skip the cleanup when V2 is enabled) so client/role/group deletion keeps working.
